QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_47

question.text: Lakshmi earns 12% on an equity mutual fund investment and is in the 30% tax bracket. Ignoring the Rs.1.25 lakh annual exemption, if her gains are taxed as long-term capital gains on equity at the current rate, what is her approximate post-tax return?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the current NISM XVII workbook (post-Budget 2024/2025), long-term capital gains above Rs.1.25 lakh on equity/equity-oriented funds are taxed at 12.5% (not 10%). Post-tax return = 12% x (1 - 0.125) = 12% x 0.875 = 10.5%. The Trap: Applying the slab rate of 30% gives 8.4% — the slab does not apply to LTCG on equity. Using the legacy 10% LTCG rate gives 10.8%, which reflects the pre-Budget rule and is no longer current. Cross-Exam Context: The 12.5% LTCG-on-equity rate above the Rs.1.25 lakh exemption is tested in NISM XVII (Retirement Adviser) and X-B (Investment Adviser Level 2).
